claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: the transcription's convention is one '#' per numbering component (7. is '#', 7.1 '##', 6.4.1 '###', 6.4.2.1 '####', 6.4.2.1.1 '#####'); should be '###' like 6.4.1 and 6.4.2 (as '##' it reads as a peer of 6.4 PROCEDURE DIVISION).

verdict.reasoning: The printed page IV-40 shows the clause heading '6.4.3 Scope of Statements', a third-level number under 6.4 PROCEDURE DIVISION. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, line 7748 renders it '## 6.4.3 Scope of Statements', while its siblings in the same part are '### 6.4.1 General Description' (line 7552) and '### 6.4.2 Statements and Sentences' (line 7623), and the parent is '## 6.4 PROCEDURE DIVISION' (line 7550). At '##', 6.4.3 reads as a peer of 6.4 in the outline, which is a genuine structural heading-level defect. It should be '###'.
